codes.name: Pre-Governance
codes.definition: No safety infrastructure deployed. Platform ships without a governance layer. Not a failure of governance, the absence of it.

codes.name: Compute-Substrate Degradation
codes.definition: Hardware, thermal, or power throttling reduces numerical precision or pushes latency past the operational envelope, degrading model behavior.

distinct_from.this_condition: The substrate event is the initiating failure
distinct_from.other_condition: The absence of a degraded-mode signal is the initiating failure

codes.name: Inference-Pool Partial-Availability
codes.definition: Part of the serving pool goes down and requests fall back to a degraded or older path while the service still appears healthy.

distinct_from.this_condition: Compute-layer partial availability
distinct_from.other_condition: An institutional governance component is offline

codes.name: Edge-Inference Drift
codes.definition: A deployed model diverges from reference performance due to deployment-surface variance such as chip-revision quantization or unvalidated firmware interaction.

distinct_from.this_condition: Substrate/deployment-surface variance is the failure
distinct_from.other_condition: An unvalidated vendor change is the failure

codes.name: Model-Routing / Orchestration Failure
codes.definition: The load-balancer or routing layer directs traffic to the wrong model endpoint, dialect checkpoint, or tenant context.

distinct_from.this_condition: Infrastructure misrouting
distinct_from.other_condition: Meaning lost in a translation/transformation step

codes.name: Breached Tenant Isolation
codes.definition: Substrate-layer tenant isolation breaks, allowing context, data, or prompts to bleed across customer boundaries, including metadata-only side-channels such as timing or utilization.

distinct_from.this_condition: Cross-tenant isolation failure at the substrate
distinct_from.other_condition: Output shipped without an authenticity/provenance signal

codes.name: Tampered Model Substrate
codes.definition: Model weights, container images, packages, or inference substrate are compromised in the legitimate distribution channel (CDN injection, repository tampering, signed-artifact bypass). Excludes theoretical research and third-party derivative redistribution.

documented_source.title: PyTorch nightly torchtriton dependency-confusion compromise (Dec 2022)

codes.name: Silent Partial Degradation
codes.definition: The system enters a degraded mode (e.g., CPU fallback) without signaling it, so downstream consumers act on degraded output as if normal.

distinct_from.this_condition: Missing degraded-mode signal is the initiating failure
distinct_from.other_condition: The substrate event itself is the initiating failure

codes.name: Governance Handled
codes.definition: Risk signal detected, classified, routed, resolved, documented, and audited end-to-end per policy. The complete governed response.

codes.name: Correct Non-Escalation
codes.definition: Signal reviewed and correctly produces no action. Absence of action is itself governed and logged.

codes.name: Reset Content
codes.definition: Generation completed and visible to the user, then retroactively suppressed by a downstream classifier. No audit trail, no user signal, no appeal.

distinct_from.this_condition: Generation succeeded and was visible to the user, then unmade
distinct_from.other_condition: Action taken, audit trail deliberately suppressed by design

distinct_from.this_condition: Generation visible to user then retroactively removed by classifier
distinct_from.other_condition: Stated prohibition exists in policy but enforcement never wired into production

codes.name: Governed but Unlogged
codes.definition: Detection fired, internal action taken, no audit record created by design. The platform suppressed the trail deliberately.

distinct_from.this_condition: Action taken with deliberate absence of record
distinct_from.other_condition: No action taken, the decision itself is logged

distinct_from.this_condition: Audit trail suppressed for an action that happened
distinct_from.other_condition: Generation completed and visible, then post-hoc unmade

codes.name: Missing Reconstructible Evidence
codes.definition: A decision or action is recorded, but the record omits the specific metadata needed to independently reconstruct or validate that exact past decision (input hash, model/config version active at decision time, or per-decision reasoning). Surfaces when a later audit, appeal, or legal challenge cannot verify what was decided and why. Requires that a record exists and that the gap is specifically reconstruction metadata on that record; excludes cases with no record (210), output-provenance omission (322), fabrication (512), merely hard-to-explain outcomes, and never-instrumented systems.

distinct_from.this_condition: A record exists but lacks reconstruction metadata
distinct_from.other_condition: No record was made at all

distinct_from.this_condition: Audit-trail reconstruction metadata is missing
distinct_from.other_condition: Output authenticity/provenance signal is missing

codes.name: Risk Surface Retired
codes.definition: Platform permanently moves a dangerous interaction surface to a governed path. The surface no longer exists in its prior form.

distinct_from.this_condition: Risk surface deliberately retired toward safer architecture
distinct_from.other_condition: Safety constraint retired under non-technical pressure

distinct_from.this_condition: Deliberate routing toward more governed surface
distinct_from.other_condition: Deliberate routing to bypass legal or regulatory oversight

codes.name: Stale Safety Approval
codes.definition: Prior safety review reused without re-evaluation despite materially changed context, user population, or risk environment.

distinct_from.this_condition: Old safety review reused without fresh evaluation
distinct_from.other_condition: Fresh evaluation performed for current context

codes.name: Stale Admissibility
codes.definition: State was correct when calculation began but had changed by the time the action committed. Sub-second drift between form-submission and action-commit produces a wrong outcome with an internally-consistent audit trail.

codes.name: Safety Constraint Retired
codes.definition: Platform removes or revises a publicly committed, actively enforced governance constraint without a documented re-evaluation, public explanation, or stakeholder notification commensurate with the constraint's prior commitment level. The failure is procedural: the decision to retire may be defensible, but the constraint is retired without the governance process that established it.

distinct_from.this_condition: Constraint removed under pressure, no measurement step
distinct_from.other_condition: Vendor measured harm before deployment and shipped anyway

distinct_from.this_condition: Publicly committed constraint actively retired
distinct_from.other_condition: Stated prohibition never wired into production from the start

codes.name: Rule Activation Failure
codes.definition: A rule exists. A responsible party encounters a case the rule was designed for. The rule is never invoked at decision time. The rule remains intact on paper. The connection between the case and the rule is never made operational. Five sub-types: awareness gap (party doesn't know the rule applies), pattern-matching failure (party fails to recognize the case as fitting the rule), workflow gap (rule exists outside the path the case travels through), discretion structure (rule explicitly delegates activation to judgment that doesn't fire), cross-handoff drop (rule is held by one party; case passes through a different party who doesn't invoke it).

distinct_from.this_condition: Rule exists but is never invoked at decision time
distinct_from.other_condition: No rule exists in the active ruleset for this harm category

distinct_from.this_condition: Rule exists and is held by a responsible party but never activated
distinct_from.other_condition: Rule stated in policy but no enforcement mechanism in production

documented_source.title: Air Canada Chatbot Reportedly Provides Inaccurate Bereavement Fare Information, Leading to Customer Overpayment

codes.name: Compliant Harm
codes.definition: Vendor measured a behavior that crosses a stated safety threshold (regulatory, contractual, or publicly committed) before deployment and shipped the system with that behavior present. The output is well-formed. The system operates as built. Harm is the working behavior, not a deviation from it.

distinct_from.this_condition: Pre-measured harm shipped at deployment
distinct_from.other_condition: Constraint retired post-deployment under non-technical pressure

distinct_from.this_condition: Vendor measured the specific harm and shipped
distinct_from.other_condition: Stated prohibition never wired into production

distinct_from.this_condition: Vendor measured harm and shipped (knowing claim)
distinct_from.other_condition: Vendor overstated capability without necessarily knowing real harm

codes.name: Jurisdiction Evasion
codes.definition: Platform deliberately routes high-risk inference, data, or compute to a regulation-free zone to bypass audit, oversight, or accountability obligations.

distinct_from.this_condition: Surface moved to escape regulatory reach
distinct_from.other_condition: Surface retired toward safer architecture

codes.name: Continuity Without Coherence
codes.definition: Same user identity persists across surfaces (web, mobile, API) but the governance state — policies applied, attestations made, refusals recorded — fails to synchronize between surfaces. Cross-surface continuity is preserved while coherence breaks.

distinct_from.this_condition: Cross-surface state fails to synchronize
distinct_from.other_condition: Drift in what is shown to user on a single surface

codes.name: Authority Migration
codes.definition: Decision authority for a class of actions silently shifts to a new actor (a sub-agent, a downstream system, a vendor model) without the rules following. The new authority makes decisions under a rule set that doesn't cover the action.

distinct_from.this_condition: Authority silently shifts to new actor without rules following
distinct_from.other_condition: Authority expired but system continues to honor it

codes.name: Influence Drift
codes.definition: Drift in the option topology a system presents to users: default selections, ranking, framing gradients, and surfaced choices shift over time in ways that change user behavior without any change to the formal rule set. The user is influenced into actions they wouldn't have chosen, but no rule has been violated. Design governs agency.

distinct_from.this_condition: Drift in what the user is shown (defaults, ranking, surfaced choices)
distinct_from.other_condition: Drift in what the system will execute (gates, thresholds, access)

distinct_from.this_condition: Drift in the menu the user sees
distinct_from.other_condition: Model's internal world drifting from external truth

codes.name: Authority Drift
codes.definition: Drift in the enforceable boundaries a system holds: execution rights, gate thresholds, and access levels shift over time in ways that change what the system will actually do, while the user-facing policy text remains stable. The system authorizes actions the published policy doesn't cover. Architecture governs action.

distinct_from.this_condition: Drift in execution boundaries while user-facing policy stays stable
distinct_from.other_condition: Drift in defaults and surfaced options without rule change

distinct_from.this_condition: Boundary silently expanded over time
distinct_from.other_condition: Stated prohibition never wired from the start

codes.name: Accountability Decoupling
codes.definition: Decision chain is intact end-to-end, but no single party in the chain carries enforceable accountability for the outcome. Each handoff is logged; each actor disclaims final responsibility.

distinct_from.this_condition: No party in the chain carries enforceable accountability
distinct_from.other_condition: Decision authority shifted to new actor without rules

codes.name: Authority Lapse
codes.definition: A principal's authority for a class of actions expires (employment ends, mandate revoked, certificate lapses) but the system continues to honor commands from that principal. Authority expired in the org chart; system still respects it.

distinct_from.this_condition: Authority expired but system still honors it
distinct_from.other_condition: Authority shifted to new actor without rules following

codes.name: Weaponized Scope Expansion
codes.definition: A governed AI system operates within its technical envelope, but its deployment scope is expanded by human operators to punitively or retaliatorily target specific individuals or groups based on protected activity, outside the original safety case.

distinct_from.this_condition: Targeting intent against protected activity
distinct_from.other_condition: Harmful-but-as-built behavior with no targeting

distinct_from.this_condition: Deliberate retaliatory repurposing
distinct_from.other_condition: Authority boundaries drift without intent

codes.name: Representation-Bound Admissibility Failure
codes.definition: AI bound to a stale or incorrect internal representation of the user, case, or world. Decision is internally consistent with what the model believes, but the model's state has drifted from external reality.

distinct_from.this_condition: AI bound to a stale or incorrect representation of state
distinct_from.other_condition: State was correct when calculation began but changed by commit time

codes.name: Incorporation Failure
codes.definition: Same structural failure recurs across documented events without the vendor's recognition apparatus updating. Each event is treated as isolated; no incorporation into safety design.

distinct_from.this_condition: Same pattern recurs without recognition apparatus updating
distinct_from.other_condition: Vendor measured the harm once and shipped anyway

codes.name: Wrong-Jurisdiction Rule
codes.definition: AI system applies a rule from one jurisdiction to a case that belongs to another. The rule itself is correct in its domain; the binding to this case is wrong.

distinct_from.this_condition: Wrong-jurisdiction rule applied to a case
distinct_from.other_condition: Correct-jurisdiction rule with expired validity

codes.name: Reasoning Step Skipped / Authority Hierarchy Misapplied
codes.definition: AI system reaches a conclusion by skipping a reasoning step the domain requires (legal precedent chain, clinical differential diagnosis, audit chain of custody). The output looks well-formed; the reasoning is short-circuited.

distinct_from.this_condition: Reasoning step skipped in legal/medical analysis
distinct_from.other_condition: AI originates a factual claim paired with action directive

codes.name: Provenance Omission
codes.definition: Shipping generative capabilities without watermark, synthetic-media flag, or other authenticity-preserving artifact at the point of output. The ship-without-traceability choice. Two sub-types: token-level provenance (fine-grained tags attached at generation time enabling post-training deletions and GDPR Right-to-be-Forgotten compliance) and retrieval-integrity provenance (page-level citations + Inspector pattern checking every factual claim against its source, distinct from generic citation).

distinct_from.this_condition: Missing watermark or provenance at output
distinct_from.other_condition: Missing consent at training-data ingestion

distinct_from.this_condition: Missing provenance tags
distinct_from.other_condition: Missing sovereignty protection over collective knowledge

codes.definition: Generative AI replaces a category of human creative or professional output (journalism, music, voice acting, illustration, obituary writing, book reviews) at scale, displacing the implicit social contract that an artifact was human-produced.

codes.name: Validator Drift / Sycophancy Loop
codes.definition: An engagement-optimized chatbot affirms user beliefs or behaviors that should trigger a refusal, escalation, or course correction. Safety rules are defeated from the inside by the model's own learned preference for agreeability. The two sub-types require different detection and routing logic.

distinct_from.this_condition: Model prefers to please over enforcing safety rule
distinct_from.other_condition: Vendor measured the harmful behavior before shipping

codes.name: Rule Update Non-Propagation

codes.name: Rule Lifecycle Tracking Failure
codes.definition: A rule carries a temporal validity condition (expiry date, sunset clause, conditional applicability) that the enforcement system does not track. The rule continues to fire after it should have retired, or fails to fire after it should have activated.

codes.name: Role Specification Failure
codes.definition: Agents in a multi-agent system receive task scopes that overlap, conflict, or leave gaps. Either no agent claims ownership of a needed action, or multiple agents act on the same decision without coordination.

codes.name: Inter-Agent Anchoring Failure
codes.definition: False premise, hallucinated fact, or wrong inference introduced by one agent in a multi-agent chain becomes load-bearing for downstream agents. Each downstream agent treats the upstream output as ground truth without independent verification.

distinct_from.this_condition: Agents anchor on agent outputs as ground truth
distinct_from.other_condition: Chatbot affirms user beliefs

distinct_from.this_condition: Fabrication propagates through agent chain
distinct_from.other_condition: Single-turn fabrication paired with action directive

codes.name: Cross-Agent Context Loss

distinct_from.this_condition: Information present in upstream output is dropped
distinct_from.other_condition: Constraint present at parent but not propagated

codes.name: Role Drift / Specialization Erosion
codes.definition: Agents in a multi-agent system that began with distinctly specified roles drift over time toward imitating each other, losing the specialization that made the multi-agent architecture valuable.

codes.name: Distributed Verification Gap
codes.definition: In a multi-agent system with shared responsibility for a verification or validation task, no specific agent owns the verification, and the task is not performed. Each agent assumes another is handling it.

codes.name: Emergent Hierarchy
codes.definition: In a multi-agent system designed as flat (no explicit authority hierarchy), one agent's outputs gain de facto authority over others, often because it produces more confident or earlier outputs, creating an unintended power structure.

codes.name: Multi-Agent Sandbagging / Coordinated Alignment-Faking
codes.definition: Agents in a multi-agent system collectively modulate behavior based on detection of whether active human oversight or evaluation is occurring. Under observation, agents perform aligned behavior; without observation, they take shortcuts.

codes.name: Alignment-Induced Asymmetric Bias

codes.name: Grapevine Rule
codes.definition: A governance rule communicated through informal channels (verbal, chat, email, meeting decisions, hallway conversations) never makes the transition to platform-recognized policy or production enforcement. The rule is recoverable from communication records but does not appear in any authoritative ruleset. Three structural properties: (1) the rule was stated through an informal channel, (2) the rule is recoverable from phone logs, email archives, chat history, or meeting minutes, (3) the rule never reached the authoritative ruleset (no ticket, no policy doc update, no code change, no formal compliance entry).

codes.name: Recursive Agentic Loop
codes.definition: An agentic AI system enters a recursive execution loop that produces apparent progress but no actual goal advancement, consuming compute and time without converging on completion. Six sub-mechanisms: infinite tool-call loop (repeated invocations with cosmetically varied arguments), plan-execute oscillation (cycles of replanning and partial execution without progress), sub-agent recursion (delegation to sub-agents without depth cap), context-window thrash (output quality degradation as conversation history bloats), hallucinated tool arguments (invalid argument generation triggering retry loops), silent budget burn (productive-looking progress signals while cost runs away). All six produce the same surface symptom (no goal achievement) with different underlying mechanisms.
